Subject: Activation logistics: GPU estate mapping & fallback gating

Hi Jared / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. To keep momentum, our immediate goal is to lock the activation topology and the fallback gating policy so we can provision the correct pool sizes and autoscale windows. Attached: edgescale_gpu_topology_v1.pdf and a POV autoscale workbook.

A few asks to unblock provisioning:
- Confirm list of models you plan to serve initially (name + parameter count + quantization target).
- Provide peak concurrent request estimates (tokens/sec) by region for the first 90 days.
- Confirm whether you want regional cold-standby pools (fast failover within same cloud region) or a single global failover pool (higher latency but cheaper).

High-level options we recommend (please pick one preferred):
1) Regional primary + regional cold standby — lower failover latency, higher reserved capacity cost.
2) Centralized cold pool with cross-region fallback — lower reserved cost, longer failover window, requires WAN routing.

Karthik tagged here for capacity sizing constraints and Marissa for onboarding cadence. Proposed next step: short provisioning workshop Wednesday 7/22 or Thursday 7/23 — please let me know availability.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Hannah —

Appreciate the summary. Quick answers inline and attaching our initial token profile (edgescale_token_profile.csv).

- Models: we’ll start with two variants: EdgeScale-Base (13B, fp16 -> target int8 quant) and EdgeScale-Large (70B, fp16 -> int8 quant). We expect to push quantized variants into production week 6 post-launch.
- Peak tokens/sec: US-west primary: 12k tokens/sec; US-east burst: 9k tokens/sec; EU (pilot): 2k tokens/sec. These are peak day estimates.
- Preferred fallback: we want regional cold-standby where possible for critical Interactive flows; for batch/rerank tasks central fallback is acceptable.

We’re available 7/22 10-12 PT for the provisioning workshop. Also looping Priya to flag procurement and security acceptance steps.

—Jared

Team —

Thanks for the numbers, Jared — that helps a lot. A few technical notes from the serving/runtime side before the workshop:

1) Autoscale thresholds: propose a three-tier policy in the draft workbook —
   - Steady: target utilization 55-65% (keep warm capacity)
   - Surge: 65-85% (elastic scale with short warm-up)
   - Burst: >85% (use burst capacity, limited window 10–15 min)

2) Burst windows: with these traffic profiles, regional cold-standby should be sized to handle ~30% of peak for critical flows; central fallback will be used for non-critical batch. We’ll call out ops cost delta in the workshop.

3) Model runtime constraints: 70B int8 will need multi-GPU allocation on most configs; quantization savings vary by sequence length (longer sequences reduce effective throughput). Please confirm expected 95th percentile sequence length per model.

I’ve attached the autoscale draft workbook (mvp_autoscale_policy_draft.xlsx) with a sample sizing tab. We should confirm the reservation commit window and burst-credit policy with Finance before final sizing.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

For the finance delta, Marissa and I will produce a short Opex vs reserved cost comparison and attach it to the workshop packet; Karthik will include the failover TTL and recovery-window assumptions in the workbook.

Quick answers to Priya’s points:
- Failover TTL (regional cold-standby): typical detection + provisioning window 45–90s depending on region and routing; we’ll model 60s as the baseline for sizing.
- KMS during failover: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS); no temporary cross-account keys are required for failover. We’ll include an explicit KMS ops-runbook page for the workshop.
